extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and writers interested in theory of imagination (Coleridge's readers and editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts theoretical criteria for using and evaluating Imagination and Fancy in poetic/creative work, plus editorial guidance about audience, method, and clarity. Focuses on Coleridge's distinctions (primary/secondary Imagination vs Fancy) and associated rhetorical/methodological advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Imagination (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The primary Imagination I hold to be the living power and prime agent of all human perception, and as a repetition in the finite mind of the eternal act of creation in the infinite."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat primary Imagination as the fundamental creative faculty — living, formative, and analogous to a divine act of creation. In evaluating work, look for evidence of this formative, world-making power rather than mere associative fancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary Imagination (definition and function)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The secondary Imagination I consider as an echo of the former, co-existing with the conscious will, yet still as identical with the primary in the kind of its agency, and differing only in degree, and in the mode of its operation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess secondary Imagination by its active, will-connected re-creative process: it 'dissolves, diffuses, dissipates, in order to re-create' and 'struggles to idealize and to unify.' It is not mere reproduction; evaluate whether the work transforms materials into unified, ideal forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fancy (definition and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Fancy, on the contrary, has no other counters to play with, but fixities and definites. The fancy is indeed no other than a mode of memory emancipated from the order of time and space...equally with the ordinary memory the Fancy must receive all its materials ready made from the law of association."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish imaginative creativity from fancy: fancy recombines pre-existing, fixed images via association and choice, but does not perform the dissolving/re-creating work of Imagination. When judging a text, flag passages that are associative cleverness (fancy) rather than organic imaginative synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match complexity to intended audience and venue
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice (as to a chapter in a volume of poems): withdraw abstruse metaphysical material from a work intended as an introduction to poems and reserve it for a specialised treatise; readers of a poetic miscellany will not expect or be prepared for a long treatise on ideal realism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial criterion: do not include highly abstruse or philosophically dense material in works whose audience expects poetry or lighter prose. If a section 'does too much, and yet not enough' and omits many links through compression, it will alienate readers and appear like fragmented steps. Place deep theory in appropriately signalled, separate publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-compression that fragments argument
rubrics_metrics.description: "You have been obliged to omit so many links, from the necessity of compression, that what remains...looks...like the fragments of the winding steps of an old ruined tower."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess structural completeness: compressed theoretical passages that omit connecting arguments should be judged as incoherent for general readers. Either expand to supply missing links or relocate the material where full exposition is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evoke sensory contrasts and revaluation (desired imaginative effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader's report of effect: alternating 'glimmer, and now in gloom; often in palpable darkness not without a chilly sensation of terror; then suddenly emerging into broad yet visionary lights with colored shadows of fantastic shapes...pictures and stone-work images...Those whom I had been taught to venerate...I found perched in little fretwork niches, as grotesque dwarfs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating imaginative writing, value capacity to produce vivid, shifting sensory atmospheres and to make familiar figures appear uncanny or newly configured. The passage's power is judged by its ability to move readers emotionally and to transfigure known names/images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague, undefined 'thing-phrases' and mystifying jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of Schelling: over-meaning or un-meaning 'thing-phrases' such as 'Licht', 'Finftemiss', 'Feuer', 'centre', 'circumference', 'ground' — either mere similes or undefined degrees of a kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style/clarity criterion: do not rely on evocative but undefined technical metaphors. If using symbolic or technical terms, define them or show their operation; otherwise they risk being mere mystification. Prefer clear definition over obscure terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological fitness: choose methods appropriate to subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation: 'An imitation of the mathematical method had indeed been attempted... Another use however is possible, namely, the actual application of the positions which had so wonderfully enlarged the discoveries of geometry, mutatis mutandis, to philosophical subjects.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for method: ensure the chosen method suits literary/philosophical aims. Blindly imitating mathematical demonstration in literary theory is likely to fail; however, selectively applying structural insights (mutatis mutandis) can be fruitful. Evaluate whether method advances intelligibility and discovery rather than obscuring it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish logical contradictions from real opposites (conceptual precision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Kantian/Schelling discussion: opposites are of two kinds — logical (absolutely incompatible, producing nonsense) or real without being contradictory (e.g., equal forces in opposite directions producing rest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In theoretical or imaginative argumentation, require precise conceptual distinctions. When authors posit opposing forces or paradoxes, check whether they are claiming logical contradiction (impossible) or real opposition (producing a third result). Misclassifying these leads to confusion; demand clear exemplification and reasoning.
